subject: Post-call: FinServ evals & recommended next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finserv.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: FinServ evals & recommended next steps

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps for running the customer-specific evals on Redwood:

1) Goals we heard
- Measure QA/document-understanding accuracy and hallucination rate on your loan-adjudication prompts
- Verify latency/throughput targets for 512-token average context in us-west region
- Compare 2 model configurations: a cost-optimized quantized variant and a higher-quality full-precision variant

2) Recommended models to include in the eval
- Llama3-70b-qlo (quantized, low-cost profile)
- Redwood-2.1-large (FP16, higher-quality baseline)
- Local baseline (your existing in-house model) — if you can provide a docker image or API endpoint we can call during scoring

3) Attached/testset & dataset format (attached: finserv_eval_testset.csv)
- Format: CSV with columns: id, prompt, expected_response, category, sensitivity_flag
- Please remove or hash any PI; if you need help we can provide a small redaction script.

4) Scoring criteria (high-level) — see attached scoring_guide.md for details
- Primary metric: Exact-match / intent-correctness (weighted 60%)
- Secondary: token-level F1 for entity extraction (20%)
- Hallucination rate (manual spot-check + model-detector) (10%)
- Latency SLA pass/fail (p95 < 350ms for interactive tier) (10%)

5) How we run this on Redwood (setup)
- We can run the eval in your preferred environment: hosted Redwood (fastest), Dedicated, or Private VPC. For regulated data we recommend Private (VPC) — you noted that during the call.
- For the eval run we ask: upload testset to a secured S3 bucket and share a short IAM role or pre-signed URL to our eval job runner (we can provide a one-time presigned upload flow).
- We’ll provide a short infra checklist (attached: redwood_eval_run_instructions.pdf) and a 60–90 minute setup call with an engineer to validate the pipeline.

6) Next steps / asks from you
- Confirm the CSV testset and the scoring weights by EOD Monday (2026-11-08).
- Approve a 60-min setup session — suggested time: Wed 2026-11-10 10:00am PT.
- If you need Private VPC for the run, confirm and we’ll loop in our security/infra to prepare a temporary private eval instance.

I’ve cc'd Neha (post-sales/solutions) to help coordinate the setup and Dev (dev_patel) for technical details.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: finserv_eval_testset.csv, scoring_guide.md, redwood_eval_run_instructions.pdf
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finserv.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finserv.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinServ evals & recommended next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our side: 

1) Data residency / logs: for regulatory reasons we need audit logs and the eval artifacts to remain in our AWS account (or behind an approved VPC). Can the eval runner write outputs back to our S3 and produce a signed log bundle?

2) PI handling: we will need to run local redaction on a subset first. Can you share the redaction script or help us run it in a staging run?

3) Scoring: who will do the manual spot-checks for hallucination rate? We’d prefer to participate in the spot-check sampling.

4) Pricing: rough estimate for a 3-model comparative eval (70b quant + Redwood-2.1 + baseline) for a ~5k example run — ballpark cost & time? We’re budgeting approvals next week.

We’re mostly good with the CSV format. Will confirm a point of contact for upload and we’d like to add Legal on the thread for a short DPA amendment.

Thanks —
Alice Chen
VP AI Products | FinServ Bank
alice.chen@finserv.com
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finserv.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinServ evals & recommended next steps

Hi Alice — quick technical notes to address the questions above. Copying the short checklist here to make setup easier: 

- Data residency / logs: Yes — we can run the eval inside your VPC/Private deployment so all artifacts (predictions, logs, checkpoints) stay in your AWS account. The Redwood eval runner supports writing outputs to a customer-provided S3 bucket and will produce a signed manifest + CloudTrail-compatible activity log.

- Redaction: attached is a small redaction helper (we can also run it in a staging job if you prefer). The CSV format you received is compatible with our runner, but ensure the "sensitivity_flag" column is set for rows with PI so we can skip those or route to an encrypted-only pipeline.

- Scoring automation: we provide the scoring scripts (python) that compute exact-match, token-F1, and a hallucination detector. For manual sampling, we’ll produce the sample set; we recommend a joint review session where your SMEs validate a 5% random sample + all flagged hallucinations.

- Cost estimate (rough): 5k examples x 3 models x avg 512 tokens — approximate compute-only cost on Hosted Redwood: $3.5k–$5k and runtime ~2–3 hours (parallelized). Dedicated/Private varies by committed capacity. We can provide a precise quote once you nominate the target deployment and concurrency.

Next steps I can own:
- Provide a pre-signed S3 upload flow and an IAM role template (I’ll share after you confirm the upload bucket).
- Stand up the eval job in Private VPC if you confirm (need VPC peering details and an approved security contact).

Regards,
Dev Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Alice — thanks for the quick review and excellent questions. Proposed immediate next actions: 

- You: confirm whether you want Hosted (fastest) or Private VPC (preferred for compliance) by EOD Monday 2026-11-08. If Private: please share contact for your infra team for a short 15-min network walk-through.
- We: Dev will send the pre-signed upload flow + IAM template and the small redaction helper.
- Scheduling: I’ll tentatively book Wed 2026-11-10 10:00am PT for the 60-min setup; will cancel/adjust if you propose another slot.
- Legal: I’ll attach our standard DPA amendment and send to your Legal contact once you confirm the run type.

If that all looks good I’ll open the HubSpot deal and hand off to Solutions for the kickoff.

Best,
Marissa
